about.title: About Us
about.subtitle: Our Mission
about.description: Discover the history and values of L'Œuvre des Samaritains
about.intro1: Founded in December 2002, L'Œuvre des Samaritains is a registered charity dedicated to food distribution in the Ahuntsic-Cartierville borough and surrounding neighborhoods of Montreal.
about.intro2: Our mission is simple but essential: to provide quality food assistance to families and individuals going through difficult times. Each week, we distribute food baskets containing fresh produce, dairy products, meats, and basic grocery items.
about.intro3: Thanks to our partners like Moisson Montréal, Centraide, and the Red Cross, as well as our generous donors and volunteers, we can help thousands of families put food on their table each year.

president.title: President's Message
president.subtitle: Our Vision
president.description: A message from our founder and president, Chantal Plouffe
president.greeting: Dear friends and partners of L'Œuvre des Samaritains,
president.paragraph1: For over 20 years, our organization has been dedicated to helping low-income individuals and families in our community. What began as a gesture of gratitude towards those who helped us during our difficult times has become a true work of solidarity.
president.paragraph2: Every week, we welcome hundreds of families to our food distribution center. More than just an emergency service, we offer a space of kindness where everyone is treated with dignity and respect.
president.paragraph3: Our team of dedicated volunteers works tirelessly to ensure that no one is left behind. Together, we firmly believe in the power of mutual aid and community solidarity.
president.paragraph4: L'Œuvre des Samaritains is more than a food bank. It's a family that welcomes, listens, and supports. Every donation, every hour of volunteering, every act of generosity makes a real difference in the lives of our beneficiaries.
president.paragraph5: I invite you to discover our history, meet our team, and join us in this beautiful mission. Together, we can nourish hope and build a more supportive community.
president.quote: We firmly believe that no one should go hungry in our community. Every act of generosity makes a difference.

mission.title: Our Mission
mission.description: The mission of L'Œuvre des Samaritains is to support low-income individuals by providing them access to a food distribution center. The organization also aims to offer listening, encouragement, and to direct people to other neighborhood resources and services that could help them.

overview.subtitle: L'Œuvre des Samaritains in 2024-2025
overview.title: A Statistical Overview
overview.point1: During the year, 900 emergency situations (free visits) and 15,000 grocery visits were served by the organization, totaling 15,900 visits from our members and non-members.
overview.point2: Since the beginning of the fiscal year on June 30, 2025, there has been a significant increase in newcomers in emergency situations.
overview.christmasText: 800 families were served over a period of 5 days.

profile.title: Participant Profile 2024-2025
profile.point1: 30% of our beneficiaries live in shared housing, given the increase in the cost of living.
profile.point2: During 2024-25: 30% of new registrations are newcomers. Since late 2024, the number of newcomers from Ukraine, Africa, and Turkey benefiting from the food bank has increased significantly.
profile.point3: Taking into account emergency situations and Christmas basket distributions: We have served nearly 17,000 free visits since 2020.
profile.point4: 17,000 free visits x $7 cost per visit = $119,000 in free visits given back to the most disadvantaged in our community.

services.title: L'Œuvre des Samaritains Services 2024-2025
services.distributionText: In 2024-2025, we received 17,000 visits. Once registered, participants receive a food basket with the help of a volunteer. Food distribution at L'Œuvre des Samaritains has been in the form of a community grocery store since its inception. To cope with the pandemic situation, we had to change our distribution procedure to adequately meet the health rules established by public health.
services.wasteTitle: B) We Say NO to Food Waste
services.wasteText: Since 2007, the organization has been environmentally conscious as we inspect and transform every perishable product that Moisson Montréal sends us. We are therefore committed to offering more products fit for consumption. This service is offered three days a week: Tuesday, Thursday, and Friday. The food offered by L'Œuvre des Samaritains is sorted, cleaned, and packaged. Offering food is important to the organization. The organization wishes to serve its clients with respect and dignity.
services.christmasText1: For the 2024 Christmas holidays, our organization was pleased to organize a food distribution for our beneficiaries. With a budget of $15,000, we were able to purchase essential products such as meat, chicken, rice, and sugar.
services.christmasText2: This initiative was made possible thanks to the generosity of our donors, who also allowed our beneficiaries to choose the items most useful to them. This support was crucial in bringing some comfort and warmth to those who needed it most during this holiday season. We warmly thank everyone who contributed to making this event a success. 800 families were served over a period of six days.

chapters.title: How Are You?
chapters.content:
In December 1999, Chantal goes to get supplies from a food bank, which she does out of necessity once a week to feed her family of 9 children. That day, one of the volunteers asks her how she is doing. She does it with such kindness and concern that Chantal opens her heart to her.

Things are not going well at all. The apartment where Chantal lives is infested with black mold, and these toxic fungi are making her whole family sick, especially the youngest ones.

Moved by Chantal's situation, the volunteer from the mutual aid organization proposes a visit to the apartment. What follows is a quick, necessary but oh so unpleasant succession of events.

Called urgently, a city inspector comes to evaluate the apartment. The verdict is clear: the house, too contaminated, is condemned and the family suddenly finds themselves on the street, a few days before Christmas.

Without a fixed address and without any belongings to their name, the family temporarily takes refuge in a small hotel room before being relocated to a shelter.

With the community rallying to help them and the media broadcasting their story on television and radio, the family eventually receives an incredible offer: a doctor particularly touched by their situation offers them a large house in Longueuil.

chapters.title: Motivated by Gratitude
chapters.content:
Filled with gratitude for all the support their family received, Chantal and her husband, Sylvain, ardently wish to give back to the community.

Supported by his family, Sylvain quickly begins the process that will lead to the creation of L'Œuvre des Samaritains, a charitable organization whose primary objective is to help the homeless.

As he has training in French cuisine, Sylvain knows exactly what he needs: pots, burners, a truck, a place to store food, a cold room, a stove, etc.

He finds collaborators, shares his project with other organizations (Moisson Montréal immediately joins the project) and obtains equipment from local businesses.

chapters.title: Feeding the Needy
chapters.content:
Two years later, in December 2002, Sylvain and Chantal's dream becomes reality. 3 to 4 times a week, at Place Émilie-Gamelin, Sylvain and his family serve good hot meals to more than 500 people.

"At first, I thought I was only feeding the homeless," confides Sylvain. He quickly realizes that this profile does not match the many people who come to receive meals. Yes, he serves homeless people but also many renters.

L'Œuvre des Samaritains gets noticed. With the media regularly talking about the organization, a new clientele shows up. The popularity of L'Œuvre brings new challenges.

chapters.title: L'Œuvre Sets Up Shop
chapters.content:
For their cause, Sylvain and Chantal transformed their garage into a cold room and the basement of their house into a pantry and industrial kitchen. The city of Longueuil is firm: the couple lives in a residential area and must therefore cease their culinary activities.

It is this zoning problem that prompts Sylvain to look for a location in Montreal. In 2005, he establishes L'Œuvre des Samaritains at 10214 rue Lajeunesse. The food distribution center now serves Ahuntsic-Cartierville.

Not receiving government aid, L'Œuvre quickly faces financial difficulties. So, one fine morning, Sylvain ties his shoes and undertakes a walk-a-thon to collect donations, covering 800 km in 35 days!

chapters.title: Same Street, New Challenges
chapters.content:
In 2007, L'Œuvre des Samaritains moves to 9413 rue Lajeunesse, in a building adequate in terms of space, but which requires a lot of maintenance. When the rains of 2009 hit Montreal, the building suffers such a significant sewer backup that L'Œuvre must interrupt its activities for a time.

Sylvain and Chantal roll up their sleeves and quickly get L'Œuvre back in operation. Their mission remains as clear as before: to meet the needs of the most disadvantaged in the community.

When Chantal becomes seriously ill in 2012, the community shows her so much support and gratitude that she is still moved by it today.

chapters.title: The Founder's Passing
chapters.content:
On December 25, 2016, Sylvain's heart, so full of love for his family and compassion for the poor, suddenly stops. He passes away surrounded by his loved ones, with an entire community sharing their grief.

The Board of Directors of L'Œuvre accompanies Chantal as they try to find ways together to keep the organization active. If Sylvain was long the heart of L'Œuvre des Samaritains, Chantal has always been its iron fist. No question for her of abandoning the project!

chapters.title: A New Chapter
chapters.content:
Since 2017, under the direction of Chantal Plouffe, L'Œuvre des Samaritains continues to grow and serve the community. Each year, we welcome more than 17,000 visits and distribute thousands of food baskets.

Our team of more than 50 active volunteers works tirelessly to ensure that every family is welcomed with dignity and respect. We have also developed strong partnerships with other organizations and local businesses.

The history of L'Œuvre des Samaritains is one of resilience, solidarity, and hope. It continues to be written every day thanks to the generosity of our donors and volunteers.
